item.title: Keepsake County review – eccentric stealing simulator with a social conscience
item.description: PC; Forward Instinct This irreverent stealth game depicts Samuel’s lonely life robbing garish, midwestern abodes – it’s a Shameless way to make a living For many people, McMansions are an eyesore, but for the protagonist of Keepsake County, a renowned burglar, they are an enticing opportunity. Prowling at purple-hued dusk, this unfussy thief is just as likely to steal a half-eaten slice of pizza or a naff ceramic ornament as he is an expensive set of golf clubs. It’s a sad, desperate way to make a living, a sense compounded by what this fledgling kleptomaniac carries his loot away in: a plastic shopping bag. Countless works have taken us to breadline America, from classic novel East of Eden to acclaimed TV crime drama Mare of Easttown. But Keepsake County is no prestige examination of the economic underbelly of the US.
